evaluationCost.note: evaluation cost; never added to arm cost

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The transfer format, the checks and the refusal order are in Summa.Storage.Transfer (Tier 2). The 'new books only' rule and the import and export transitions are in Summa.Web.Engine.Accounting (Tier 2). The wire (Tier 3) only maps kernel events to Msg cases (`"booksTransferRequested", (fun _ _ -> BooksTransferRequested)`) and decides nothing. The GitHub guard uses the existing `onGitHub model` predicate.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Transfer.fs is pure; its own comment says 'Pure.' and it writes JSON by hand so it avoids System.Text.Json. The clock arrives through `ctx.Now`. The download is requested as data (`OfferDownload(name, "application/json", Convert.ToBase64String(...))`) and the save as the existing `save` effect (`SaveBooks`). Nothing new is performed below Tier 4.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The supported version is defined as `Version` but `read` matches a separate literal `1M`. The timestamp format string is written once for export and once for read. The copies agree today but can drift apart. Everything else has one definition: the schema literal, `Exports.Classification`, `Exports.dataVersion` and `Codec.dateText`.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The contents counts (`contentsOf`), the content-mismatch check, the version 1 and 2 handling and the preview wording and pluralisation are all in Summa.Storage.Transfer (Tier 2). The engine only projects `Transfer.preview model.BooksTransferText` into the view value. The HTML only binds `data-text="booksTransferPreview"`.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effects were added. `contentsOf` and `preview` are pure functions in Tier 2. The follow-up adds no new I/O, clock or randomness.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have a single authority, `contentsOf`, which export, read and preview all use. The file-version numbers are still restated as literals (`1M | 2M`, `declared = 1M`) next to the `Version` constant. The preview formats the export date itself with "yyyy-MM-dd", while the existing import notice in the engine uses `Codec.dateText`. The timestamp format is also still duplicated between `stamp` and `read`. All copies agree today.
